prompt_text: I need new tires installed in Pleasanton. Which specific tire shops should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can narrow it to the exact shops, but first a couple quick questions so I recommend the best places for your situation:

- Which Pleasanton do you mean (Pleasanton, CA or Pleasanton, TX)?  
- What vehicle (make/model/year) and wheel/tire size (if you know it)?  
- Any preferences: brand, budget, same‑day install, membership (Costco), run‑flat or performance tires, winter tires?  

If you want an immediate, general answer, call one shop from each of these categories — they cover the most common needs:

1) Warehouse club tire center (e.g., Costco Tire Center) — Why call: very competitive prices on name brands, routine promotions, and consistently good warranties/road‑hazard coverage for members. Ask about membership requirements and total out‑the‑door price (mounted, balanced, taxes, disposal).

2) Large national tire retailer (e.g., Discount Tire or Tire Rack partner shop) — Why call: biggest in‑stock selection of brands and sizes, good price matching, and often quick same‑day installs. Ask about availability of your exact size, price match policy, and whether they do TPMS relearns if you have sensors.

3) Full‑service chain garage (e.g., Firestone Complete Auto Care, Pep Boys) — Why call: they handle installation plus alignment and other car services in one stop. Good if you suspect you’ll also need an alignment, brakes, or have warranty work. Ask whether alignment roll is included or available same day and the cost for mounting/balance.

4) Independent/local tire shop in Pleasanton — Why call: personalized service, often willing to match or beat national prices, quicker scheduling, helpful for older vehicles or custom wheels. Ask about road‑hazard protection, lifetime rotation/balancing policies, and whether they can mount low‑profile or run‑flat tires.

What to ask every shop when you call:
- Exact total out‑the‑door cost per tire (include mounting, balancing, new valve stems, tire disposal fee, taxes).
- Whether TPMS relearn is included and cost (if applicable).
- Road‑hazard warranty and length of treadwear warranty.
- Availability for same‑day or next‑day installation.
- Whether alignment is recommended/included or available that day.
- Whether they dispose of your old tires and if there’s an extra charge.

If you confirm which Pleasanton and your vehicle or tire size, I’ll give 4–6 specific shops in that city with phone numbers and a short note about each (fastest scheduling, best price, best warranty, best for performance tires, etc.).
